text:
Situation: Corvale East has 8.5 days of furosemide 10 mg/mL 2 mL injection on hand. Corvale Lakeside holds 28 days and Corvale General holds 18–19 days of the same strength and volume. Tablet and other injection strengths at all sites exceed two weeks. The FDA shortage for furosemide injection has been current since 2020-04-07.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the furosemide injection shortage on 2020-04-07 and it remains current as of 2026-10-21. FDA inspected Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited (FEI 3004011473) and classified the inspection OAI on 2019-09-06, 214 days before the shortage posting. FDA later issued an OAI classification letter to Intas dated 2023-04-05 and published import alert 66-40 on 2023-06-01 for the same firm. FDA inspected Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) and classified the inspection OAI on 2019-09-06, with the classification letter dated 2020-05-25, 48 days after the shortage posting.

Our position: Internal transfer is the fastest way to extend Corvale East coverage while preserving two weeks at the sending site. External purchases are available from suppliers not on the FDA shortage list, but their labels do not identify manufacturing plants we can verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 33 vials of furosemide 10 mg/mL 2 mL from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
2. If additional supply is needed, transfer 53 vials of furosemide 10 mg/mL 2 mL from Corvale General to Corvale East — requires pharmacy director approval of the transfer request.
3. Evaluate purchase from Amneal Pharmaceuticals LLC, Camber Pharmaceuticals Inc., or Civica Inc. — requires buyer execution after confirming plant information.

Not recommended: Delaying transfer while awaiting new purchase orders; relying on tablet inventory to cover injection needs.
